snippet.title: What If the Moon Disappeared? 🌙 You Have 1.3 Seconds
snippet.description:
If the Moon vanished right now, you'd still see it for 1.3 seconds. After that, things go wrong fast: tides, nights, animals, even the length of your Monday. 🌙

One year without the Moon, or one week without the Sun? Tell us in the comments 👇

SOURCES
• The Sun's tidal force is about half the Moon's: NOAA https://oceanservice.noaa.gov/education/tutorial_tides/tides02_cause.html
• Day length about 1.4 billion years ago (around 18 hours): Meyers & Malinverno, PNAS 2018 https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.1717689115
• The Moon stabilizes Earth's tilt: Laskar, Joutel & Robutel, Nature 1993 https://doi.org/10.1038/361615a0 (how large the effect would be is still debated)
• The Moon recedes about 3.8 cm per year: NASA https://eclipse.gsfc.nasa.gov/help/ApolloLaser.html
• Light takes about 1.3 s to cross the Moon's ~384,400 km (distance divided by the speed of light)
• Coral spawning follows the Moon's cycle, along with water temperature and day length: Australian Institute of Marine Science (aims.gov.au)
